pages.title: A new way of living
pages.alt: Timber chalet on wheels with large windows and a raised roof

pages.title: From Ron’s experience to building a company.
pages.alt: Assembly of a chalet’s timber structure
pages.intro: Chalet to Go is at the beginning of its organisational development. The experience behind it belongs to Ron Lima, with approximately 25 years in construction and chalet development.
pages.body: Work in the United States, Brazil and Switzerland connects two distinct stages: learning to build and organising a company able to manufacture, sell and deliver. Today’s project draws on that journey, with the Brazilian operation’s first unit as the next concrete step.
timeline: In Miami, Ron develops Belo Horizonte Construction.
Back in Brazil, Ron starts producing small chalets. An order for 18 units highlights the need to organise capacity and operations.
Projects of different sizes broaden operational experience and precede the plan for a base in Jura.
Prepare Brazilian production and present the Swiss operation to investors and the Municipality of Delémont.

pages.title: Precision in making. Nature in living.
pages.alt: Façade, cladding and window details of a timber chalet
pages.intro: Wood is the starting point. Care at every stage turns a material into a place to live.
pages.body: Chalet to Go combines timber construction, standardised components and freedom to personalise. Dimensions, equipment and finishes can be adapted to the use and market of each project.
features: Material selection, drying and preparation are part of construction quality.
Repeatable components to organise production, assembly and transport.
Insulation and energy solutions considered according to the needs of each development.

pages.title: Small in scale. Rich in possibilities.
pages.intro: Natural light, wood and efficient use of space. The aim is to bring together the essentials in settings that welcome different ways of living.
images: Bright kitchen and open living area with a mezzanine
Bedroom beneath a timber roof with windows
Timber chalet interior with natural light

pages.title: One idea. Different ways to live.
pages.intro: From a compact unit to a housing development. The planned range accommodates different uses, scales and levels of personalisation.
pages.alt: A group of small timber chalets on wheels
models: A compact chalet or standardised tiny house.
A modular chalet for family or tourism use.
Multiple units and shared spaces, designed as a project.

pages.title: The next chapter starts here.
pages.alt: A professional working on a building’s roof
pages.intro: Minas Caixa, Belo Horizonte. A team ready to build and sell the first unit of this new stage.
pages.body: The Brazilian operation brings together physical and digital infrastructure, workforce organisation and commercial preparation. This practical work progresses alongside the project’s presentation in Switzerland.
features: The facility in the Minas Caixa neighbourhood will be the base for building and selling the first unit.
Preliminary agreements and expressed interest are in place, with land prepared for project development.

pages.title: From the first unit to a production process.
pages.intro: Building the first unit starts the Minas Caixa operation. To repeat that delivery, the plan sets out a sequence from defining the model to installation on the customer’s land.
pages.body: The proposed Jura workshop combines manufacturing, assembly, covered storage and display. Timber selection follows each base: Brazilian species for the domestic operation and Swiss timber for the planned establishment in Jura.
steps: Model, dimensions, equipment and finishes according to use.
Select, dry and prepare timber and components.
Assembly and quality control before delivery.
Check dimensions, weight, access and any need for disassembly.
Coordinate with local professionals and destination requirements.
pages.risk_body: Purchases and timelines depend on the approved project. Materials, labour and transport belong in the budget; deposits and staged deliveries are part of the proposed cash management. Expansion through distributors depends on demonstrated manufacturing and support capacity.

pages.title: From Delémont, a vision for the world.
pages.alt: A landscape of mountains, forest and green fields
pages.intro: The canton of Jura is the intended base for designing, manufacturing, demonstrating and distributing modular homes.
pages.body: The priority is to present the dossier to Swiss investors and the project to the Municipality of Delémont. The plan includes a workshop with assembly, storage and showroom areas, connected to local suppliers and professionals.
features: Establish the production base and develop the first customers and partnerships.
Expand gradually with distributors and installation partners.
Assess exports and international projects according to capacity and local requirements.

portrait.title: Interest in the first units
portrait.body: Marc Mathys has expressed personal interest in buying Chalet to Go’s first 15 units. This interest is part of the project’s commercial outlook; it is neither a contracted order nor secured revenue.
portrait.caption: Marc Mathys · personal purchase interest

pages.title: More than units. Places to meet.
pages.intro: The ecological village vision expands the project’s scale: homes, shared spaces and a closer relationship with the setting.
pages.body: The plan’s pilot concept envisages 8 to 20 units, green areas, shared spaces, water management and energy solutions. Each development depends on technical design, partners and local conditions.
features: Prepared land, preliminary agreements and expressed interest in developing an ecological village.
Prepared land and expressed interest also exist here. Scope and schedule are still to be defined.

pages.title: Grow on a solid foundation.
pages.intro: A gradual establishment, with production capacity and team size following the growth of orders.
milestones: Validate the plan, organise implementation and seek financing, a workshop and a prototype.
Develop initial sales and contracts for series production.
Advance industrialisation, the European market and preparation of the pilot ecological village.
Broaden models, distribution and international projects as demand develops.

pages.title: From assumptions to results.
pages.intro: Starting the business means estimating how much each unit contributes towards overheads. Sales volume and each year’s fixed costs then determine the possible result.

pages.title: Housing and training, at a future stage.
pages.intro: The dossier describes an intention beyond sales: combining temporary shelter with training in woodworking, electrical work, plumbing and construction. The proposal seeks to provide housing and skills useful for rebuilding communities.
pages.body: The material reports an initial experience started during the pandemic and interrupted by international restrictions. A restart would depend on governments, organisations and partners; no current programme is confirmed.
pages.concept_body: The concept envisages an institutional purchase accompanied by an equivalent unit for donation. Before committing, funding for the extra unit, logistics and training must be defined. These donations are excluded from sales and earnings projections.

pages.title: The task now is to turn the plan into deliveries.
pages.intro: The priorities are to build and sell the first Brazilian unit, develop the Natal initiative and present the Delémont establishment to investors and the Municipality.
pages.body: Portugal, European expansion and social programmes are subsequent possibilities. Progress depends on initial operating results, formalised projects and the capacity to finance them.

finance.budget_note: Figures from the reference PDF for the Swiss establishment. The sum has been checked; items still require quotations and a location. These are not incurred expenses or secured funds.
finance.scope_note: This budget concerns the Swiss operation. It must not be added to Brazilian costs or deducted in full from each year’s operating result.
finance.projection_intro: Starting the business means estimating how much each unit contributes towards overheads. Sales volume and each year’s fixed costs then determine the possible result.
finance.projection_note: Selling prices and production costs are provided. Annual results still require capacity, fixed expenses and other variable costs. Enter these assumptions; no volume is filled in as guaranteed sales.
finance.required: Complete all fields with operating assumptions.
finance.invalid: Check the inputs: valid numbers, whole units and annual sales within declared capacity.
finance.no_breakeven: No break-even with nonpositive unit contribution
finance.capacity_warning: Break-even volume exceeds the declared annual capacity.
finance.table_caption: Annual projection in the selected currency
finance.formula: Result = units × (selling price − variable cost) − fixed costs.
finance.note: Price and variable cost remain constant over three years. Sales inputs are assumptions, capped at monthly capacity × 12, not contracts. Fixed costs should include fixed salaries, payroll charges, rent and administration; variable labour belongs in unit cost without double counting.
finance.exclusions: Before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortisation. This is not net profit, available cash, investor return or investment payback. The scenario excludes land purchases, donation revenue and currency conversion.
finance.method_title: What the numbers can tell us
finance.method_body: The initial budget shows uses of funds; revenue measures sales; earnings depend on costs. The PDF’s revenue curve cannot establish earnings. This projection therefore calculates by unit and year, showing losses when costs exceed sales.
finance.print_note: Scenario calculated from reader-entered inputs; not a company-approved forecast.
finance.balance_note: Selling price less production cost. Other expenses are not deducted; this is not net profit.
finance.supplied: Prices and costs supplied by the team in September 2026.
finance.scenarios_note: Conditional scenarios for 1, 5 and 15 units of a single model. These are neither annual targets nor confirmed sales. The model mix of a possible Marc Mathys purchase is undefined.
finance.currency_note: Amounts in CHF, without conversion. Production costs include labour, transport and installation, as confirmed by the team. Sales tax treatment remains to be defined.
finance.forecast_note: Selling prices and production costs are provided. Annual results still require capacity, fixed expenses and other variable costs. Enter these assumptions; no volume is filled in as guaranteed sales.
